title: Cool-Cap Ledger: Indoor Temperature Evidence for Landlords
one_liner: Low-cost sensors and tamper-evident logs that give landlords, tenants and inspectors one accepted reading of indoor temperature.
customer: Owners and property managers of 10+ unit buildings in Maryland (80F cap since June 1 2026), LA County (82F from Jan 1 2027) and NYC (78F cap, owner duty from 2030). Tenant groups and code enforcement are secondary buyers.
problem: Cooling caps are enforced by complaint, so the fight will be over readings: a tenant's phone app against a landlord with no record. Landlords face fines and habitability suits with no defensible data, and tenants cannot prove violations.
solution: $30 sensors in a sampled set of units, third-party-verifiable logs, a tenant-visible dashboard, automated compliance reports and a dispute-response pack. An upsell is a unit-level cooling-gap map for capex planning, showing which units to retrofit first under LA County's phase-in.
why_now: Maryland's cap is already live, LA County starts in about 3 months, and NYC Local Law 2026/023 is passed. The summer 2026 heat set off a wave of complaints.
revenue_model: $4-8 per unit per month for landlords, plus municipal enforcement licenses.
non_obvious_insight: In a complaint-driven regime, evidence is the product. Neutral data protects landlords from false claims and tenants from real violations, so both sides will accept it.
first_30_days: Sign 5-10 LA County and Maryland property managers for winter pilots ahead of the Jan 2027 start. Build the logging and report pack, and pilot in 100 units.

title: Exoskeletons That Delay Tradesperson Retirement
one_liner: Lease passive and powered exoskeletons with fitting, coaching and outcome-based pricing to shops and insurers, targeting 55+ tradespeople whose retirement drives the labor gap.
customer: Workers' comp carriers and PEOs, contractor associations, and 10-100 employee roofing, plumbing, HVAC, framing and drywall shops with aging crews.
problem: ABC says most of the 349K 2026 shortfall is retirements, and older tradespeople leave over knees, backs and shoulders. Replacement hiring is impossible in a market where trade-school enrollment hype is called a demographic mirage. Strain injuries also drive comp claims.
solution: Vetted kits (passive shoulder and back supports, emerging powered hip and knee assists), professional fitting, a task playbook for overhead, attic, roofing and crawlspace work, and usage and injury-risk telemetry. Monthly lease with a guarantee tied to comp premium reduction or absence rates, piloted with carriers first.
why_now: Powered assist suits have fallen from tens of thousands of dollars to low thousands per unit. Comp carriers face margin pressure and want proven loss-control tools. The retirement wave now dominates the labor gap, and hiring cannot fill it.
revenue_model: $150-300 per worker per month lease, a carrier program fee, and outcome-based rebates.
non_obvious_insight: This is a retention and insurance business, not a robotics business: the cheapest new journeyman is the 62-year-old who did not retire. The buyer with the incentive and the loss data is the comp carrier, not the worker or the owner.
first_30_days: Approach two regional comp carriers or PEOs with a 60-day pilot. Sign three shops (10 workers total) and measure discomfort, absences and adoption. Secure wholesale terms with one exoskeleton supplier and one trade association endorsement.

title: Market Surveillance for Entertainment Prediction Markets
angle: Pairing 2: Gaming, entertainment, live experiences, fandoms x Cybersecurity, deepfake fraud, identity verification, scams targeting consumers and businesses
one_liner: Sportradar-style integrity monitoring for the boom in prediction-market contracts on awards, charts, box office and game releases, where insiders and bot farms can swing outcomes.
customer: CFTC-regulated prediction-market exchanges and brokers that list entertainment contracts (Kalshi-type venues and the betting and brokerage firms entering the space). Secondary buyers are rights holders and award bodies (studios, labels, game publishers, guilds) that want to know when their confidential information is being traded.
problem: Per the briefing, Kalshi went from about $11B to $22B valuation in 2026, entertainment and awards are already about 11% of its activity, and states are fighting the venues. Exchanges must list contracts that are not readily susceptible to manipulation and run surveillance, but their tooling is built for sports and finance. Entertainment outcomes can be moved by insiders (PR staff, awards accountants, streaming-platform employees, contractors who know game release dates), by bot-farmed streams and votes, by review-bombing, and by leaked builds and schedules. Resolution sources (Spotify charts, Rotten Tomatoes, Steam counts, box office) are each gameable in a different way.
solution: (1) A 'contract risk review' done before an entertainment market lists: score the resolution source for manipulability (cost to swing it, for example streams or votes needed) and the insider population (who knows the outcome and how many people), then recommend rules such as delayed settlement, position limits and source hierarchies. (2) Live surveillance that flags anomalous trading, such as fresh accounts trading ahead of announcements or positions timed with leak or stream-spike signals, cross-referenced with external manipulation indicators (streaming bot networks, vote farms). (3) Investigation and referral packages for exchanges and regulators. (4) A rights-holder subscription that alerts when a contract references their confidential events.
why_now: Kalshi's valuation doubled in five months and new entrants are listing culture contracts. Multiple states are attacking event contracts, so demonstrable surveillance is now a legal-defense asset. GTA VI launches 19 Nov 2026 and Q4 award season and Spotify Wrapped create dense culture-contract activity. AI-cheap bot streaming and vote farms lower manipulation costs, and Chainalysis notes scam tooling now sells for about $50 (per briefing).
revenue_model: Annual retainer of $60-250k per exchange for the surveillance feed. $2-10k per contract risk review. Rights-holder alert subscriptions of $2-5k/month. Hourly investigation and expert-witness work.
non_obvious_insight: Sports-integrity firms never learned how an awards accountant or a streaming intern leaks, and entertainment insiders are far more numerous and less regulated than athletes. Resolution sources are commercial dashboards, not referees. The buyer's budget is really a legal-defense budget for defending the product state by state.
first_30_days: One fraud/market-abuse analyst plus one music/film/game data specialist. Publish a 'manipulation cost' analysis of the 10 most-traded entertainment contracts (Oscar categories, Spotify top artist, Steam concurrent players, Rotten Tomatoes scores) and send it to compliance heads at 5 exchanges. Offer a 30-day paid pilot review of upcoming contracts (GTA VI launch, award season) at $10-15k.

title: Royalty-Paying Archive of Master Tradespeople's Hands
one_liner: Pay retiring master electricians, pipefitters and welders to record expert egocentric video with think-aloud narration, license it to robotics companies, and share royalties with the workers.
customer: Robotics and embodied-AI companies building construction, maintenance and data center installation robots, and foundation-model labs. A second buyer is apprenticeship programs and trade schools, which can license the annotated footage as curriculum.
problem: Egocentric data for robots is being commoditized at the bottom: in September 2026 reporting, gig workers earn about $3-10 an hour filming dishwashing and folding laundry. Expert tasks, like reading a bad splice or feeling a torque, are rare in the data, and the people who know them are retiring, which is also the labor shortage the AI buildout depends on.
solution: Recruit 60+ year-old tradespeople through union retiree halls. Pay $60-120 an hour to wear head and wrist cameras (plus IMU gloves) on real jobs with owner consent, and to narrate why they choose each action and how they detect problems. Add edge-case tagging by a second expert. Blur faces and PII. License datasets by the hour, and pay each worker a royalty of 10-20% of license revenue and a residual on repeat licensing.
why_now: In 2026 papers such as EgoHumanoid showed that robot-free human egocentric demonstrations can train humanoid manipulation directly, so human video is now a working input. The commodity layer is crowded and cheap, so expert-conditioned data is the next premium. Labor and IP disputes over gig data are also starting, which makes a royalty model a moat.
revenue_model: License $150-600 per hour of expert-annotated footage (a hypothesis to test in pilots), exclusivity premiums, and pre-paid data collection contracts. Secondary revenue from trade-school curriculum licenses.
non_obvious_insight: Robotics' bottleneck is shifting from quantity to tacit expertise, and tacit expertise is a wasting asset because its holders are retiring. A royalty share turns those workers from data laborers into stakeholders, which is a legal, ethical and recruiting advantage the $3-an-hour vendors cannot copy.
first_30_days: Recruit 15 retired electricians and pipefitters via IBEW and UA retiree halls and local Facebook groups. Get two robotics startups to pre-pay $25-50k each for 100 hours. Equip people with a $400 kit and a one-page site consent and PII-blur workflow. Deliver the first 20 hours with narration and get a written reference from each buyer.

title: Owner-Download: Capture Tacit Knowledge Before Sale
one_liner: Passively capture 60-90 days of an owner's calls, messages and jobs into a transferable playbook and a question-answering agent for the buyer.
customer: Owners aged 58+ of owner-dependent service and professional businesses ($300k-3M revenue) planning a sale in 12-36 months, plus the brokers who list them and the buyers who acquire them.
problem: Buyers discount hard for key-person dependency. The knowledge sits in the owner's head and phone: pricing instincts, customer quirks, vendor favors, unwritten rules. The traditional six-month handover rarely captures it.
solution: With consent, capture call recordings, texts and email, invoices, calendar and short weekly AI interviews. Produce SOPs, customer memory cards, learned pricing and quote logic, vendor scorecards and 'if X breaks, do Y' runbooks. The buyer gets a Q&A agent for year one ('how did the owner price gutters over 40 feet?') and the package goes in the data room as a transferable asset.
why_now: Long-context models, cheap call transcription and agentic retrieval make passive capture practical. Loosened SBA financing (up to $10M combined from July 2026) is drawing more first-time buyers who need this.
revenue_model: $2,500-6,000 per owner, broker referral fees, and a $199/month buyer subscription to the Q&A agent for 12 months.
non_obvious_insight: AI did not make this possible by automating the work but by making capture passive, so an owner no longer has to stop working to write manuals. Key-person discount is measurable, so the package can be priced against it.
first_30_days: Recruit five owners through two brokers in one vertical (HVAC, plumbing or landscaping). Run the capture pilots and ask buyers to rate the packages against a control listing on confidence and price.

title: App-Diet Service for the Phone-Upgrade Freeze
one_liner: As phones get unaffordable, today's handset becomes a five-year handset, so old-device performance decides who keeps users.
customer: Banks, wallets, telcos and government digital services with large user bases on 2-3GB RAM Android phones in Africa, India and LatAm.
problem: Memory-driven price rises are stretching replacement cycles. Bloated apps crash on old devices, and churn from that is invisible in analytics.
solution: A fixed-price audit on a real farm of used 2GB phones on 2G/3G. Deliver sub-10MB lite builds and WhatsApp or USSD fallbacks, then a monthly regression retainer. The wedge is a four-week audit for one mid-tier bank or wallet.
why_now: Memory is 30-40% of phone cost, LatAm shipments fell 10%, and GSMA's $40 phone pilot shows the price problem.
revenue_model: $15-40k per audit and $5-10k per month for device-lab monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone forecasts the next phone. The second-order effect is that the current phone lasts far longer, so performance on old hardware, not features, drives retention.
first_30_days: Buy 15 used phones and publish a teardown of the top 10 fintech apps in Nigeria or India. Use it to book audits.

title: Pharmacy-Side PBM Ledger for Employers
one_liner: Independent pharmacies hold the half of the PBM ledger that employers never see, which is what the PBM actually paid the pharmacy. Pool it to run spread audits for self-insured employers, and give pharmacies a stay-or-leave calculator for their take-it-or-leave-it PBM contracts.
customer: Two sides. First, independent pharmacies, at $99-199 a month for benchmarking and a network-contract modeler. Second, self-funded local employers, school districts, counties and union funds (from 100 to 5,000 lives), plus the benefit consultants and TPAs that serve them, who pay per audit or a share of verified savings.
problem: The employer sees only what it paid the PBM. The PBM sees both sides and hides one. The pharmacy sees what it was paid and what it paid the wholesaler, but has no benchmark and no idea whether the network offer that arrives every Q4 for January 1 is worse than its peers' terms. Everyone negotiates blind. PBMs threaten a pharmacy with losing about a quarter of its business if it declines, and a plan sponsor cannot verify 'pass-through' claims.
solution: Read-only ingestion of the pharmacy's 835 remittance files and invoice costs from its pharmacy management system (PMS). Output 1) per-drug, per-PBM reimbursement benchmarked against NADAC and an anonymized peer pool. 2) A stay-or-leave model of each 2027 network offer built from the pharmacy's own claims mix. 3) With sponsor consent, a claim-level tie-out of the pharmacy-paid amounts against the employer's PBM claims file. That yields a true spread and rebate pass-through gap in dollars per member, delivered as an audit the employer can use to renegotiate or move to a transparent PBM.
why_now: The contract season for January 2027 is happening right now, which gives a hard deadline and a free entry wedge. Employer fiduciaries are under pressure from ERISA suits over PBM costs, state PBM transparency laws and FTC scrutiny. Pharmacy closures (Rite Aid gone, Walgreens closing about 1,200 stores) have given local officials political will. OCR and LLM parsing of messy remit PDFs now makes onboarding a one-day job rather than a consulting project.
revenue_model: Pharmacy subscription of $99-199 a month, or free in exchange for data. Employer audit fees of about $8k-25k per mid-size sponsor, or 10-20% of first-year verified savings. Data licenses to state employee plans, attorneys general, employer coalitions and consultants at a higher tier.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone in the PBM fight holds half a ledger, and only the pharmacy can prove the gap. Thirty pharmacies in one county reconstruct the local school district's and county government's spread at claim level. Independents will hand this data over willingly because it is the first ammunition they have ever had against take-it-or-leave-it contracts.
first_30_days: Recruit 15 pharmacies through the state independent pharmacy association with the pitch 'we will model your 2027 PBM offers free'. Build parsers for the three biggest PBMs' remit formats (the 835 EDI standard helps). Deliver the first stay-or-leave reports. Hire a healthcare attorney to structure data-use terms, since provider-manual confidentiality clauses and HIPAA de-identification are the main risk. Offer one local school district or county a free pilot spread audit and turn the result into a one-page case study.

title: Craft Data: Retiring Machinists Teach Robots
one_liner: Pay shops to let experienced craftspeople wear cameras and gloves, and sell the captured factory-floor skill data to robot-learning labs.
customer: Robot foundation-model and humanoid companies buying training data. Shops are the second customer, receiving cash and auto-generated standard work instructions.
problem: Physical AI funding hit $18.6B in Q2 2026, but labs lack high-quality real-world industrial manipulation data (setups, fixturing, deburring, measuring by feel). Meanwhile a retiring workforce takes unrecorded tacit skill, and no dataset of it exists.
solution: An egocentric capture kit (head and wrist cameras, instrumented glove, audio narration) worn during normal work. Add job context from CAM programs and travelers. Deliver curated, annotated datasets to labs. Shops receive setup videos, SOPs and a training library, and workers share in revenue, with consent, IP and safety protocols agreed up front.
why_now: Record physical-AI funding, cheap wearable capture hardware, imitation-learning advances, and a retirement wave. Labs need real industrial data, not lab data.
revenue_model: Target $150-400 per curated hour from labs (to validate with first buyers). Pay shops about $40 an hour. $500 a month per shop for the SOP and training library.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input to robot learning is expertise, not compute. The same footage is a shop's best defense against retirement knowledge loss, so shops will host the capture and even pay for the by-product.
first_30_days: Recruit five shops with free SOP videos as the hook. Capture 100 hours. Pitch five labs with samples. Aim for one paid pilot of $20-50k. Hire an employment lawyer for consent and IP terms.

title: Borrowing-Base Verification for Recycler Lenders
one_liner: A drone-and-assay 'borrowing base as a service' that lets specialty lenders finance recyclers against verified inventory.
customer: Asset-based lenders, factoring firms and specialty commodity funds (primary payers), plus recyclers who need working capital against bales, black mass, swarf and scrap.
problem: After Ascend's Chapter 11, Li-Cycle's bankruptcy and the PET reclaimer closures, credit for recyclers is tight. Lenders cannot verify what is in the pile: volume, grade, moisture, title and price risk. Commodity-finance frauds, shrink and theft are a real concern.
solution: Monthly drone and LiDAR volumetrics, density and grade sampling, scale-house data integration, title and lien checks, and index-based mark-to-market. Lender-ready certificates with shrink alerts.
why_now: The 2025-26 recycling failures made lenders cautious, while BIS-driven domestic feed flows and price volatility make inventory more valuable and more mispriced.
revenue_model: $1.5-4K per site per month, plus basis points on facilities placed.
non_obvious_insight: Recyclers are not short of collateral; lenders are short of trust in it. Collateral management firms serve large metal traders and skip the $5-50M recyclers.
first_30_days: Talk to 10 ABL lenders and 2 factoring firms. Pilot with 3 recyclers refinancing now. Build a volumetrics pipeline on off-the-shelf drones and photogrammetry.

title: White-Label Camera Forensics for Cities and Schools
angle: Pairing 2: Reshoring, tariffs & automation x Government / defense / municipal
one_liner: Scan municipal and school camera, recorder and IoT fleets to unmask white-labeled hardware with covered Hikvision or Dahua internals and produce grant-ready compliance attestations and phased replacement plans.
customer: City and county IT and police departments, school districts, transit agencies and the MSPs and integrators serving them. They pay $3-15k per fleet audit plus an annual monitoring fee.
problem: Federal grant terms (DOJ, DHS and FEMA, school-safety programs) bar covered surveillance equipment under NDAA Section 889 and 2 CFR 200.216, including where it is a substantial or essential component of a system sold under another brand. Many fleets bought 2015-2020 contain OEM boards nobody can trace, and the integrator who sold them has a conflict in saying so. Sensor stacking (noise detectors on license-plate readers) is spreading while surveillance-vendor scrutiny grows.
solution: An agentless scanner that fingerprints devices by firmware, banners, MAC ranges and cloud endpoints (including peer-to-peer relay services) to reveal OEM lineage across cameras, NVRs, access panels and doorbells. Output is an asset inventory, a grant-attestation letter, and a replacement plan sequenced against grant cycles, with domestic or trade-compliant alternatives. Integrators pay a referral fee for replacement work.
why_now: Compliance is now BOM-level across industries, and grant conditions are being enforced more tightly. Cities face ADA Title II (Apr 2027) and CJIS 6.0 (Oct 2027) deadlines that already force IT audits. Public backlash over camera vendors makes proof of diligence politically valuable.
revenue_model: $3-15k per fleet audit, $1-3 per device per year for monitoring and re-scan, and 3-8% referral fees on replacement projects. Sell through MSPs and state cooperative contracts.
non_obvious_insight: Compliance is defined by the chip in the box, not the label on the box. Origin lineage of white-labeled OEM electronics is an unpriced supply-chain data problem that only shows up at the moment a city touches federal money, and the fingerprint database becomes the moat.
first_30_days: Release a free 'Is my camera a Hikvision?' desktop scanner for IT staff as lead-gen, audit 3 school districts at cost to build the fingerprint set, and then sell $5k audits to the first 5 districts via grant writers and state school-safety offices.

title: Exosuit-as-a-Service Paid by Workers' Comp Carriers
one_liner: Rentable powered back-and-hip assist suits for home-care aides and nursing assistants, with usage data that earns workers' comp premium credits.
customer: Home-care agencies and nursing-home operators with high workers' comp experience mods, workers' comp carriers and MGAs with loss-control budgets, and PEOs.
problem: Aides and nursing assistants have some of the highest musculoskeletal injury rates, and a claim costs tens of thousands. Agencies can't install ceiling lifts in clients' homes, and with 77-80% turnover, injuries drive both cost and churn.
solution: Rent-by-month lightweight powered assist suits with sizing, training and warranty. Onboard sensors count bends and lifts to build injury-risk analytics for the carrier, who credits premiums. Start with clients who need transfers, and use it as a retention perk.
why_now: Consumer-priced powered exosuits appeared in 2025-26, and workforce scarcity makes worker safety and retention perks valuable. Comp carriers are actively looking for loss-control programs in a squeezed home-health margin environment.
revenue_model: $60-100 per suit per month paid by the agency or shared with the carrier, performance rebates, and an analytics subscription.
non_obvious_insight: Sell to the party that pays for injuries (the carrier), not the aide, and let data turn a gadget into a premium negotiation. Lab claims of strain reduction still need real-world proof, which the pilot supplies.
first_30_days: Lease 30 suits from an OEM, find two agencies and a regional comp carrier, and run a 90-day trial measuring injuries, lost workdays and turnover.

title: Screw-Pile Foundations That Skip the Concrete Crew
one_liner: Engineered helical-pile foundations with torque-logged QA and prefab floor cassettes, installed in a day, for spec homes, ADUs and factory-built homes where foundation crews are booked out for weeks.
customer: Spec and production builders in crew-constrained markets (Texas, Florida), ADU builders and factory-built home dealers.
problem: Foundations sit 30+ days waiting for crews, and loan interest keeps accruing while 15-20 houses wait 6+ weeks. Forming, pouring and finishing are crew-dependent and hard to automate. Chassis-free factory homes need light foundations that are quick to install.
solution: A foundation-only subcontractor installing helical piles with a torque-monitoring logger and structural details pre-approved by a partner engineer for three soil regions, plus a prefab insulated floor cassette or steel grade beam. Torque logs become an objective, timestamped QA report for inspectors and lenders. Autonomous pile driving, already proven in solar, is the roadmap.
why_now: Enforcement and labor shortages are stretching foundation crews. Autonomous pile-driving rigs are commercial in solar. Chassis-free homes and the ADU boom create demand for light foundations. Lenders and inspectors increasingly accept digital QA data.
revenue_model: Priced roughly at parity with slab or stem-wall per home and sold on speed, with margin from utilization. Per-sq-ft or per-home pricing, plus licensing engineered details to other installers.
non_obvious_insight: Changing the design removes the scarce trade from the critical path entirely. Insiders try to hire or automate concrete crews, but a foundation with no forms, no cure time and no finishers becomes a machine-and-engineering task with objective logs.
first_30_days: Engage a geotech and a structural PE for standard details. Rent a mini-excavator with a torque head. Sign two builders with stuck lots or ADUs, install three foundations, and document schedule savings versus their alternatives.

title: Vacant-House Concierge for Parents Moving Into Care
one_liner: One monthly plan that insures, inspects, maintains and eventually sells the house left empty when a parent moves to memory care or dies.
customer: Adult children and executors (45-65), often out of state, acting under POA or as executor. The channels are elder-law and estate attorneys, memory-care sales directors and senior move managers.
problem: When a parent moves into care, the house sits empty for 3-12 months. Homeowners policies typically restrict coverage after 30-60 days of vacancy, and pipes, taxes, utilities, break-ins and mail scams pile up. Probate cases rose about 32% from 2020 to 2024, and exhausted heirs are unprepared.
solution: A $199-449 monthly plan: vacancy-compliant insurance via an MGA partner, weekly inspections with water, temperature and entry sensors, autopay of utilities, taxes and HOA from an estate or POA account, seasonal maintenance, mail forwarding, sibling portal, documentation for the estate accounting, then cleanout, staging and a sell-when-ready referral.
why_now: The 80+ cohort is growing about 36.6% over the decade, senior housing is at 90% occupancy so moves happen in crises, and the $6T wealth transfer is underway. Heirs are far-flung Gen X executors who need a service, not a checklist.
revenue_model: Monthly subscription, insurance commissions, cleanout and staging fees, and a referral or flat fee on the eventual sale.
non_obvious_insight: Estate-settlement startups start at death, but the costly, uninsured window opens at the care move, years earlier. Anchoring on that moment gives access to the family before competitors and before the house loses value.
first_30_days: In one metro dense with senior housing, recruit 10 estate and elder-law attorneys and five move managers, secure a vacancy-insurance MGA quote, and sign the first 10 homes at an introductory rate.

title: Hardware-Origin Audits for Drones and Robots
angle: Pairing 2: Logistics and physical automation x Trust and verification markets (lens: proving quality and provenance)
one_liner: Teardown-level bill-of-materials and firmware audits that prove what is really inside a 'US-made' drone or robot, sold to small makers, to the public-safety and utility buyers who must prove compliance, and to insurers.
customer: US drone and robot makers with 5-100 employees selling to public safety, utilities, agriculture and federally funded programs. Buyers: county, city and state procurement offices and grant recipients. Insurers and lenders who need 'no covered components' assurance.
problem: The FCC barred new DJI and Autel models in Dec 2025, US drone tariffs took effect in Sep 2026 with component tariffs in 2027, and China's export controls cover motors, batteries, radios and sensors. Buyers must show they bought compliant gear, but suppliers self-declare, rebrand and reroute. Procurement staff cannot inspect a flight controller. After the IEEPA tariff-refund saga, customs origin claims will draw scrutiny. Unitree G1 at about $16k tempts robot buyers into the same problem.
solution: An auditor plus registry. Teardown-level BOM verification (identify chips and modules, firmware and network-callback tests for covered-vendor endpoints, cross-check of supplier declarations and customs documents). It produces a signed origin and compliance dossier per model and lot. A public registry lets procurement staff query a model against state and federal restrictions.
why_now: The FCC action, tariffs and Chinese export controls all landed between Dec 2025 and Sep 2026. Domestic supply is emerging (Amprius won a $75M award for 500 Wh/kg cells), and dozens of new entrants all claim 'American-made'. A number of state laws also restrict agencies from buying Chinese drones (specifics to verify).
revenue_model: $8k-$30k per product audit for makers. $1k-$3k per re-certification on a BOM change. $2k-$5k/yr buyer-side registry subscription for agencies. Lot-level spot-check fees. Referral fees from insurers.
non_obvious_insight: When a ban creates a market, the scarce asset is belief in compliance, not the compliant product. The audit fee is a tax on every new entrant, and buyers fear being embarrassed by an audit finding. Inputs are cheap (a bench, a spectrum analyzer, firmware tooling) and one engineer can produce the first audits. The same dossier doubles as customs-origin evidence.
first_30_days: With maker consent (or from public teardowns), audit 5 currently marketed 'American-made' drones and publish the methodology. Offer three small US makers a $5k pre-audit with a money-back guarantee. Sell 3 full audits at $10k-$15k. Pitch a state public-safety procurement association on the registry.

title: Co-op Childcare Kits That Also Make Parent Friends
angle: Pairing 2: Mental health, loneliness and community x Parenting, childcare deserts and kids/AI/screens
one_liner: Modern rails (licensing map, insurance, shift scheduling, lead-teacher placement) that let 12-20 neighbor families launch a parent-participation preschool or aftercare co-op in a few months, cutting tuition and curing parent isolation at the same time.
customer: Groups of 10-20 families in childcare deserts: new-parent groups, neighborhood and church parent groups, remote-work households, employer resource groups. Later: employers and HOAs that sponsor co-ops.
problem: Childcare averages $13,128 a year and the labor inside that price is the reason. Parents are lonely (friendship is now a measured health metric), and post-2020 new parents often have few local friends. Parent co-ops once made childcare 30-50% cheaper, but they withered because launching one requires legal, licensing, insurance and payroll expertise that volunteer boards lack.
solution: 'Co-op OS': a state-by-state navigator showing where parent-participation programs are exempt or lightly licensed (verify per state), template bylaws, an insurance bundle (general liability plus abuse-and-molestation), background checks and mandated-reporter training, a shift scheduler that assigns parent duty days and keeps a credit ledger, payroll for one paid lead teacher, and a lead-teacher matching service for displaced educators. Friendship is designed in: monthly parent-only dinners, a crisis buddy system and meal trains.
why_now: Dependent-care FSAs now reach $7,500 and the 45F credit lets sponsoring employers offset 40-50% of childcare costs. Hybrid schedules and AI-driven job churn have left many parents with flexible hours to trade for tuition. Parents are already organizing collectively on phones and schools, so collective action is normalized.
revenue_model: About $1,500 setup, $149/mo per co-op for software and payroll, insurance commissions, a lead-teacher placement fee of about $2,000, and employer sponsorship of co-op slots.
non_obvious_insight: Time is the new money. Childcare is expensive because it is labor, and co-ops swap parent hours for tuition. Nobody does it because of coordination and compliance, not desire. Parent friendship is the retention engine, not a nice-to-have, and lonely parents recruit each other for you.
first_30_days: Pick two states with clear parent-participation rules. Recruit 3 existing neighbor or parent Facebook groups into a 4-week 'Co-op Launch Sprint' with a $299 deposit per family. Engage an early-childhood attorney for templates and an insurance MGA for the bundle. Place one lead teacher and aim to have three co-ops running by January 2027.

title: Advancement Ledger for Parents Funding Jobless Kids
angle: Pairing 1: AI labor-market disruption x Death, estates and the great wealth transfer
one_liner: A living ledger plus a state-specific estate addendum that records what Boomer parents advance to struggling adult children, so the inheritance later comes out fair and siblings do not end up in court.
customer: Parents aged 65-80 with $500K-$5M estates and two or more adult children, at least one of whom is unemployed or underemployed. Channel: estate attorneys, elder-law firms and RIAs, who white-label it. Payers: parents ($199 setup plus $12-20/mo), firms ($500/mo white label) or RIAs (per-household fee).
problem: The AI hiring freeze (NY Fed: recent-grad underemployment about 42%) turns Mom and Dad into the bank of last resort. Rent, tuition, car and 'bridge loans' flow unevenly to siblings, undocumented and undecided as gift, loan or advancement against inheritance. Decades later, executors and trustees face contested history and estate litigation, and families break. Wealth advisors say family meetings are essential, yet nobody tracks advances.
solution: Parents log each advance in a simple app and tag it as gift, loan or advancement. The child e-acknowledges it. Optional interest at the AFR turns it into a formal promissory note. The system flags amounts near gift-tax-return thresholds (annual exclusion about $19K). It produces a running equalization statement the attorney can attach to a will or trust with a state-specific 'hotchpot' clause. An annual sibling-transparent 'family statement' replaces secrecy. Repayment or forgiveness schedules kick in when a child gets re-employed.
why_now: Millions of 22-35-year-olds face a low-hire market while Gen X and Millennial heirs are about to receive trillions (Cerulli: Gen X about $14T in the next decade). Federal student-loan caps reportedly tightened from July 2026 (verify), pushing more tuition onto family money. With a higher federal estate exemption (reportedly about $15M per person from 2026, verify), fewer estates are tax-driven and more are conflict-driven, so fairness documentation is now the main planning value.
revenue_model: $199 'Fair Share Package' (memo, ledger, 45-minute attorney review). $12-20/mo subscription. Attorney and RIA white label at $500/mo per firm or a per-household fee. Later: paid mediation add-on when siblings disagree.
non_obvious_insight: The AI jobs shock will show up in probate court a decade before it shows up in most statistics. Unequal parental support is the seed of the next generation of estate fights, and equalization is a data problem (a ledger), not a legal one. Parents will pay real money to keep their kids from fighting after they die.
first_30_days: With two friendly estate attorneys, draft an advancement memo and equalization clause for two states. Put up a landing page aimed at parents searching 'paying rent for my 26-year-old' and post in personal-finance and parenting communities. Sell the $199 package with a manual spreadsheet ledger to the first 25 families, then build the app around what they actually log. Ask 10 elder-law attorneys to co-present at seminars.

title: Fees-in-Kind: Harvest Becomes School Fee Credit
one_liner: A weigh-in and ledger service that lets parents pay school fees with maize, beans and potatoes at a transparent price, while schools get cheaper, steadier food supply.
customer: Boards of management, principals and bursars of public boarding and day secondary schools, including the new senior-school cohorts, plus rural private schools. The end users are smallholder parents in maize, bean and potato zones.
problem: Farm households are asset-rich and cash-poor exactly when fees fall due in January, May and August. Schools already accept 'a tin of maize' informally, but the value is whatever the storekeeper or bursar decides, with no receipts. Meanwhile the same schools buy food through brokers at inflated tender prices, and government capitation often arrives late. Children still get sent home over arrears even when the parents' store is full of grain. Food is often the largest line in a boarding school's budget.
solution: A Fee Credit Ledger. Farmers deliver graded produce to the school store or a village collection point. A standard weigh ticket (photo of the scale plus a moisture reading) generates an SMS receipt, and the value is credited to the learner's fee account at a published reference price such as NCPB or the county market average, minus a small handling margin. The school gets a weekly reconciliation. On the buying side, the platform, registered as an AGPO-eligible youth or women group (check how each school's procurement committee applies the 30% reservation), bids for school food supply and sources from the same parents. It pools, grades and quality-checks (moisture, aflatoxin spot test). An add-on is hermetic storage bags on credit so parents can deliver later in the term rather than dumping at harvest.
why_now: The first CBC cohort entered senior school in January 2026, expanding boarding and food demand, and the next cohort arrives in January 2027, so schools are planning Term 1 supply now. Capitation delays keep squeezing school food budgets. Cheap Bluetooth scales, moisture meters and M-Pesa and SMS receipts make a trustworthy weigh ticket trivial. Principals in Kenya talk in tight associations, so one working pilot spreads fast.
revenue_model: A 4-8% handling margin on food flow: schools pay below their current broker-inclusive price and farmers receive above the broker price. Later a per-learner per-term ledger fee (about KES 50-100). Once the ledger produces credit-quality data, short-term financing of fee arrears or school receivables.
non_obvious_insight: In every rural ward the school is the largest, most predictable institutional food buyer, and the 'fee arrears list' is a timing and valuation mismatch, not poverty. Fintechs treat barter as embarrassing or informal, but for smallholders paying in maize is the default. What is missing is fair valuation and a ledger everyone trusts. The AGPO set-aside is an under-used entry ticket for farmer groups into school tenders.
first_30_days: Sign 2-3 principals through your own old high school or a heads' association branch meeting for a one-term pilot in January 2027. Buy two Bluetooth hanging scales and moisture meters (a few hundred dollars), run the ledger on Google Sheets plus Africa's Talking SMS, and recruit 100 parent households at PTA meetings. Set the price at the midpoint between the farmgate broker price and the school tender price. Register the entity for AGPO and open a supplier profile with the school.

title: Recovering Tariff Surcharges Small Buyers Already Paid
angle: Pairing 1: SMB back office/compliance/marketing/succession x Trust & verification markets (compliance recovery x forensic audit)
one_liner: Contingency-fee forensic audits of supplier invoices that find the explicit 'tariff surcharge' lines small retailers, contractors and restaurants paid in 2025, and turn them into evidence packets while importers hold the refund money.
customer: Small retailers, contractors, restaurants, salons and small manufacturers that bought from distributors who itemized tariff surcharges. Fee is about 25% of recovery. Secondary customers are mid-size distributors that received IEEPA refunds and want a defensible pass-through rebate calculation.
problem: The Supreme Court ruled on 2026-02-20 that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs. CBP says about $166B is refundable to 330,000+ importers of record, with about $81B paid by July 2026. 76% of firms that source internationally passed costs to customers, so downstream small buyers paid the tax and get nothing directly (brief inference). Brokers and trade lawyers chase the importer's refund, not the payer's claim.
solution: The owner forwards a supplier-invoice mailbox or QuickBooks export. Document AI extracts surcharge lines and products, identifies the likely importer of record, calculates the claim, and packages evidence (invoice, surcharge wording, date, refund status) into a demand letter. A partner consumer-protection or commercial firm handles aggregated claims and arbitration. Distributors get an audit-trailed rebate module for voluntary pass-through.
why_now: The refund flow is happening now (CAPE launched by April 2026, 2,000+ suits filed), importers hold the cash, and downstream invoice records and claim windows decay every month. Document AI makes invoice-level extraction cheap. The IEEPA ruling is a one-time event, so the window is finite.
revenue_model: 25% contingency on recovered amounts, split with counsel. Add SaaS fees from distributors for rebate audits.
non_obvious_insight: Explicit surcharge line items are invoice-level admissions that the charge existed to cover a tax later refunded, which makes these claims far stronger than generic price-increase complaints. Distributors want to keep small customers, so a clean evidence packet often converts to a negotiated credit without litigation. Claim strength varies by contract and state and needs counsel, so the business is forensic evidence assembly, not legal advice.
first_30_days: Build the invoice parser on 50 sample invoices and offer free surcharge scans to 30 members of one trade association (independent hardware, bike or restaurant-supply buyers). Identify the 10 most frequent surcharging distributors, sign a contingency-split agreement with a law firm, and target first negotiated credits by month 3.

title: NFC Open-Item Tags for Aircraft Shift Handover
one_liner: Tamper-evident NFC red-tags that record every opened panel, disconnected line and removed component on an aircraft, and block sign-off until each is closed with an as-left photo.
customer: Directors of maintenance, quality and safety managers at regional airlines, Part 145 shops, Part 135 fleets and helicopter EMS operators. Line stations with 3-6 techs per shift are the beachhead.
problem: The most dangerous moments in line maintenance are shift change and interruption. A tech opens a panel, disconnects a connector or leaves a cap loose, gets pulled to an AOG, and hands over verbally or with a sticky note. The 'system' is a paper red tag, a whiteboard and memory. The 2024 737 MAX 9 door-plug investigation put undocumented removal of fasteners in front of every director of maintenance. Digital task cards do not fix this, because the physical state of the aircraft between task steps is not captured anywhere.
solution: Tamper-evident NFC tags that hang on the physical thing that is open. A tech taps the tag with a phone (offline-first, because hangars have dead zones), records what, why and who, and hangs it. At handover, the app shows a manifest of open tags by tail. The aircraft cannot be released in the app until every tag is closed with an as-left photo. Export goes to the work order as PDF or CSV on day one, and to the maintenance system through an API later. Techs get a time-stamped record of exactly what they did and left.
why_now: The 2024 door-plug event made undocumented maintenance a board-level topic. The FAA's 2024 SMS final rule expanded safety-management obligations to more operators, and safety departments are looking for concrete evidence-capture tools. NFC-capable phones are standard and cheap tags are commodity, so the hardware cost is pennies. AI is a minor part of this, which is a feature. It ships without data-science risk.
revenue_model: Per-aircraft subscription ($75-150 per tail per month) plus consumable tags at $0.50-1.50 each, the razor-and-blade model that made lockout-tagout a large industrial category. Enterprise tier with maintenance-system integration and safety analytics.
non_obvious_insight: Maintenance software dies at the tech's hands, because anything that adds keystrokes gets skipped. This replaces a paper red tag with something faster, and it gives the tech a personal alibi for their own certificate if something is questioned years later. The buyer is quality and safety, not IT, so it needs no integration with the maintenance system to start. Underneath the software is a consumables business.
first_30_days: Ask your own director of maintenance to pilot it at your line station, so you can test it during real shift changes. Build a progressive web app with offline storage and buy 2,000 off-the-shelf NFC stickers. Run a free 30-day pilot at two line stations and one Part 145 shop, then measure tags closed with photo, handover time and missed items caught. Convert the pilot to $99 per tail per month plus tags, and use the measured near-misses as the sales collateral for safety managers.

title: Independent Leakage Audits for Age Verification
one_liner: A red-team lab that measures how easily under-16s slip past each platform's age check (VPN, borrowed ID, face tricks) and sells defensible evidence to platforms, counsel and insurers.
customer: Mid-size social, gaming and video platforms operating in Australia, the UK, Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia and US ban states. Also their outside counsel and, later, regulators.
problem: Insiders treat age assurance as a vendor-selection problem. Regulators judge whether 'reasonable steps' were taken. Australia is investigating five major platforms (fines up to A$49.5M) and proposed in June 2026 to double fines to about A$99M and reach app stores and age-assurance providers. By February 2026 many children had already bypassed the ban. Vendors self-report accuracy but nobody independently measures real-world leakage at the 14-17 border.
solution: A standard test harness of about 20 evasion scenarios (VPN region switch, parent's ID, older-sibling account, face-estimation edge cases, re-registration). It runs with consented adult testers and synthetic profiles, never with minors. Outputs are a quarterly public 'Leakage Index' plus confidential 'reasonable-steps evidence packs' and a continuous monitoring subscription.
why_now: Bans went live between December 2025 and June 2026 and enforcement is starting. The proposed extension of liability to age-assurance providers means everyone in the chain wants third-party evidence. The reported IDScan breach and Persona complaints (both from the brief, one flagged shaky) push platforms to question their vendors.
revenue_model: Confidential audits at $15-60k each. Monitoring subscription at $3-10k a month. Later, licensing the test protocol to regulators and insurers.
non_obvious_insight: This is an assurance market like SOC 2, not a technology market. The buyer wants a defensible paper trail, and it must be independent of the vendors it grades, so the lab should be paid by the platforms rather than the vendors.
first_30_days: Write the 20-scenario protocol with a regulatory lawyer. Run it on 5 public age gates in Australia using adult test accounts, keeping to what counsel clears. Publish a free 'Leakage Index' teaser. Cold-email trust-and-safety leads and regulatory counsel at 40 mid-size platforms with their own results.
